native_result.query: In which millenium did amber had the highest value and in what time interval did it peak?
native_result.HypoA: Amber has historically high and stable values in the 4th millenium BCE. with its all time peak around 3300 to 3000BCE.
native_result.HypoB: Amber reached its highest value in the 4th millennium BCE (4000-3001 BCE), and the peak occurred in the contiguous time interval CE -3300 to CE -3000 (calBP 5250 to 4950; 301 consecutive 1-year rows; 3300-3001 BCE), where the Z value of Amber hits its global maximum of 1.54. Cross-corroborated by the raw Amber anchors (CE -3300, -3200, -3100, -3000 = 1.54) and by the independent Zamber series in capital.csv (max 1.54 at BCE 3300-3000, cultural period MN). The wider elevated envelope (Amber > mu+1 sigma approx 1.045) is a single contiguous block CE -4016..-2958, which contains the strict plateau.
native_result.WorkflowB: Primary signal = Amber_inter in data/time_series_data.csv (1-year grid, 3601 rows, fully populated). Verified Amber_inter matches raw Amber (sampled every 100 years) at every anchor -> Amber_inter is faithful step interpolation, not smoothing. Grouped rows into 1000-year bins using CE // 1000 and summarised (max, mean, n) per bin; bin CE // 1000 = -4 (CE -4000..-3001 = 4th mill. BCE) had both the highest max (= 1.54, tied with bin -3) and the highest mean (1.488), decisively beating neighbouring millennia. Located global max Amber_inter = 1.54 and identified contiguous 1-year block attaining it -> rows 800..1100, CE -3300..-3000, calBP 5250..4950 (301 years). Computed mu and sigma of Amber_inter (= 0.0860 and 0.9591) and defined an elevated band at > mu+1 sigma = 1.0451; this set is a single contiguous block rows 84..1142 -> CE -4016..-2958 (calBP ~5966..4908), strictly containing the plateau. Cross-check 1: raw Amber anchors (rows 0, 100, ..., 3600) all == Amber_inter at those indices; raw Amber = 1.54 at CE -3300/-3200/-3100/-3000. Cross-check 2 (independent source): capital.csv Zamber decoded (decimal comma -> float); max = 1.54 at BCE 3300/3200/3100/3000 (CE -3300..-3000), cultural-period group MN -- exact match to the plateau rows. Millennium convention used (stated to pre-empt BCE off-by-one): N-th millennium BCE = [N*1000 .. N*1000-999] BCE; thus 4th mill. BCE = 4000..3001 BCE = CE -4000..-3001, which is the bin containing the plateau interior.
